highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.152.0 adds Graphite GPU rendering and backend-neutral asynchronous pixel readback.
highlights_body: The Skia m152 release also brings a Silk.NET Vulkan helper, explicit-font rendering on Nano Server, and fixes for pixel, iterator, and uniform-buffer lifetimes. Existing Ganesh APIs remain available and unchanged.

bullets.detail: Updates the bundled renderer to m152 and VulkanMemoryAllocator to 3.4.0, retaining the Vulkan allocator fallback used by SkiaSharp callers.

bullets.lead: Native rendering and cache lifetime corrections
bullets.detail: Includes upstream Ganesh stale-readback and font-rendering stability fixes, m152 servicing updates, and a SkCachedData correction that releases its mutex guard before deleting the object.

Adds contexts, recorders, recordings, textures, and image caching for Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn, including browser WebGPU. Use the explicit record/snap/insert/submit model; shipping Graphite surfaces require asynchronous pixel readback rather than synchronous ReadPixels.

SKImage and SKSurface.RequestReadPixels provide rescaled RGBA readback. Results are callback-scoped: copy data out to retain it. Raster callbacks run synchronously; Ganesh completion requires submission and CheckAsyncWorkCompletion. Failure returns a null result.

Adds SkiaSharp.Vulkan.Silk.NET with GRSilkNetBackendContext and typed extension initialization, and makes GRVkExtensions constructible. The package is included in production packing; the SharpVk helper remains available.

bullets.lead: Iterators and pixmaps retain their backing owners
bullets.detail: Region iterators keep their source region alive. ExtractSubset and WithColorType/WithColorSpace/WithAlphaType pixmaps retain the ultimate pixel owner, preventing collection while native views still reference its memory.

bullets.lead: Owned buffers and consumed streams are released promptly
bullets.detail: Frees the allocated pixel buffer when SKImage.Create fails, disposes the previous uniform data on Reset, and disposes consumed non-memory-backed stream assets when their HarfBuzz blob is released.

bullets.lead: Streaming data output avoids an intermediate copy
bullets.detail: SKData.SaveTo writes the native buffer directly on span-capable targets instead of copying each chunk through a managed buffer. .NET Framework and netstandard2.0 retain the buffered path.

Null-terminated text encoding avoids an intermediate string. SKFourByteTag and HarfBuzzSharp.Tag formatting avoid character boxing, and Font.Shape reuses caller-provided feature arrays rather than copying them.
Pre-sizes runtime-effect uniform lookups and caches invariant wrapper-registration reflection checks instead of repeating that work during object setup.

bullets.lead: Load explicit fonts on Nano Server
bullets.detail: The Nano Server native build uses FreeType so typefaces loaded from files, streams, or data can render. It still has no system-font discovery; applications must load their fonts explicitly. Normal Windows builds retain DirectWrite.
Adds Apple dSYM symbol packages without adding symbols to customer runtime packages, and gives both Android native libraries deterministic build IDs tied to their split-debug files.

contributor_summaries.jeffska: Enabled FreeType-backed loading of explicit fonts on Nano Server
contributor_summaries.mmitche: Reduced Windows native build overhead by initializing the MSVC environment once per build
contributor_summaries.ramezgerges: Introduced Graphite GPU backend bindings for Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn

preview_summaries.v4.152.0-preview.1.1: Preview 1 introduced Graphite, asynchronous RGBA pixel readback, the Silk.NET Vulkan helper, and Nano Server explicit-font support. It also fixed region-iterator and pixmap backing-owner lifetimes.
preview_summaries.v4.152.0-rc.1.26426.14: Release Candidate 1 restored production packing of the Silk.NET helper, added Apple native symbol packages and deterministic Android symbol identity, and reduced shaping and tag-formatting allocations.

harfbuzz_summary: Font.Shape reuses caller-provided feature arrays, and Tag.ToString avoids character boxing. Apple native symbol packages and deterministic Android build IDs improve native diagnostics without changing the bundled HarfBuzz 14.2.1 engine.

v4.152.0-preview.1.1.headline: Preview 1 introduced Graphite, asynchronous pixel readback, Silk.NET Vulkan helpers, Nano Server font loading, and source-lifetime fixes.

v4.152.0-rc.1.26426.14.headline: The release candidate reduced shaping allocations, fixed uniform-buffer and blob-stream cleanup, restored Silk.NET package production, and added native debugging assets.

v4.152.0.headline: SkiaSharp 4.152.0 finalizes the release with a cached-data lifetime correction.
v4.152.0.body: The native mutex guard is released before its owning cached-data object is deleted.
